tells.2: Template-perfect section scaffolding (Why now / Rationale / Risks and mitigations / Financial summary with [$X] placeholders), though the prose itself reads naturally
tells.3: Repeated 'Mitigation:' labels and uniform parallel bullet structure that feel auto-generated
tells.4: Bolded lead-in phrase on every list item plus stock phrasing like 'enhanced in-store experience' and 'I'm happy to walk through'

reason: Version 1 is clearly human but rambling, vague and repetitive ('successful in closing the stores'), so it is weak for leadership. Version 2 keeps the strong structure and specifics of 3 and 4 but writes the mitigations as plain first-person commitments ('We will...'), which reads as the most credible and least templated.
